audit_findings.title: The earnings anchor and balance-sheet bridge use different acquisition perimeters
audit_findings.magnitude: $98.8 million cash consideration; Kiwi contributed $37.3 million of six-month revenue and a $5.2 million net loss including acquisition amortization
audit_findings.mechanism: The pre-Kiwi owner-earnings anchor excludes the acquired business, while the post-Kiwi cash bridge reflects the purchase payment; Kiwi earnings, working capital, acquired liabilities, and integration costs therefore are not aligned with the bridge.
audit_findings.evidence: As consideration for the Kiwi Acquisition, the Company paid approximately $ 97.2 in cash to the Kiwi Seller Parties.
audit_findings.explanation: This is a demonstrated perimeter mismatch, not merely a possible risk. The $98.8 million transaction is larger than the $74.1 million owner-earnings anchor, and Kiwi's reported revenue and loss show that the omitted operations are economically significant. Direction is mixed because adding Kiwi's operating cash earnings may increase value, while losses, integration costs, and working-capital requirements may reduce it.
audit_findings.action: Rebuild owner earnings on a post-acquisition trailing-twelve-month basis or value Kiwi separately, reconcile acquisition-related working capital and liabilities, normalize acquisition amortization and integration costs, and rerun all scenarios.

audit_findings.title: The full cash balance may not be surplus or freely distributable to common equity
audit_findings.magnitude: $127.0 million, equal to $0.88 per share of intrinsic value and $0.61 per share of the 30% MOS threshold; removing it reduces base value from $8.07 to approximately $7.19 and buy-below from $5.65 to approximately $5.03
audit_findings.mechanism: Cash is added dollar-for-dollar in the equity bridge; any operating, restricted, covenant-support, or otherwise unavailable cash must be excluded from that addition.
audit_findings.evidence: Legal and contractual restrictions in agreements governing our indebtedness, as well as our financial condition and operating requirements, may limit our ability to receive distributions from Janus International Group, LLC and its respective subsidiaries.
audit_findings.explanation: The filing demonstrates restrictions can exist but does not establish how much of the $127 million is unavailable, so the amount of error remains unresolved. The scale is material because removing the full addition would put the approximately $5.03 buy-below threshold below the $5.09 market price, changing the purchase conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain entity-level cash, restricted-payment capacity, covenant calculations, minimum operating liquidity, integration funding needs, and foreign accessibility; replace $127 million with verified surplus cash and rerun the bridge.

audit_findings.title: Variable-rate interest risk is not explicit in the growth scenarios
audit_findings.magnitude: $5.5 million annual pre-tax interest change per 100 basis points, equal to 7.4% of the $74.1 million owner-earnings anchor
audit_findings.mechanism: Because interest remains in equity-level owner earnings, future SOFR movements directly alter owner earnings and its growth path rather than being handled through a separate debt deduction.
audit_findings.evidence: Taking into account the SOFR floor of 1.00%, a hypothetical increase or decrease in 100 basis points of the SOFR rate on the amounts outstanding under the First Lien Term Loan as of January 3, 2026, would have led to an approximate $5.5 increase or $5.5 decrease in the interest expense of the First Lien Term Loan on an annual basis.
audit_findings.explanation: The variable-rate exposure and filed sensitivity are demonstrated, while the future rate path is uncertain. A 100-basis-point movement is substantial relative to the anchor and would compound through the forecast and terminal value. Higher rates overstate the present valuation; lower rates understate it.
audit_findings.action: Confirm the July 2026 debt balance, 2.00% SOFR margin, floor, and any hedges, then rerun bear, base, and bull cases with explicit after-tax SOFR paths and corresponding interest expense.

audit_findings.title: Positive growth assumes the latest volume and pricing erosion is cyclical
audit_findings.magnitude: Base-to-bear equity-value difference of $252 million or $1.74 per share; the corresponding 30% MOS threshold falls from $5.65 to approximately $4.43
audit_findings.mechanism: The cyclical-normalization assumption enters the owner-earnings growth rates and therefore affects every forecast year and terminal value.
audit_findings.evidence: The organic revenue decline for the year ended January 3, 2026 is 75% attributed to the overall decline in volume with the residual 25% decline being attributed to price associated with uncertainty in the economic and interest rate environment.
audit_findings.explanation: Whether the weakness is structural remains unresolved, but deterioration is already present: six-month organic revenue declined 4.5%, adjusted EBITDA declined 16.2%, and second-quarter organic revenue declined 6.0%. Selecting the bear rather than base growth case would move the buy threshold below the $5.09 market price, so the assumption can change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Obtain subsequent order intake, backlog, like-for-like pricing, utilization, project-financing conditions, market-share data, and organic margins; rerun growth cases using evidence-supported stabilization or continued-erosion paths.

audit_findings.title: The anchor depends materially on judgmental percentage-of-completion estimates
audit_findings.mechanism: Cost-to-complete revisions alter recognized revenue, contract margins, working-capital balances, and consequently the owner-earnings anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Changes in the percentage of completion assumptions could have an impact on recognized service revenues.
audit_findings.explanation: The use of judgmental estimates and the auditor's critical-audit-matter designation are demonstrated, but no identified misstatement or adverse true-up is supplied. Exposure is meaningful—43% of first-half 2026 revenue was recognized over time and contract assets rose from $27.6 million to $38.7 million—but the record cannot quantify any owner-earnings correction or establish its materiality.
audit_findings.action: Review contract-level post-period true-ups, margin fade, cost-to-complete revisions, contract-asset aging, loss provisions, disputed change orders, and historical estimate accuracy; rerun the anchor if a net correction is established.

audit_findings.title: The latest annual anchor contains an extra operating week
audit_findings.magnitude: Pro-rata normalization is approximately $1.4 million, or 1.9% of the $74.1 million anchor; it would reduce base value by approximately $0.14 per share and buy-below by approximately $0.10 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: Treating 53 weeks as a recurring year modestly inflates normalized owner earnings and all forecast cash flows derived from the anchor.
audit_findings.evidence: Fiscal year 2025, ending on January 3, 2026, and fiscal year 2024, ending on December 28, 2024, were comprised of 53 weeks and 52 weeks, respectively.
audit_findings.explanation: The 53-week fiscal year is demonstrated, while whether the anchor was already normalized is unresolved. Even assuming earnings accrued evenly and removing one fifty-third, base buy-below would remain approximately $5.55, still above the $5.09 market price; this does not change the valuation conclusion.
audit_findings.action: Verify the anchor worksheet for a 52-week adjustment and, if absent, remove the actual extra-week owner earnings or apply the pro-rata $1.4 million normalization.
